items.caption: This oracle-script redraw has a narrow upright stroke with branching arms above a lower enclosure that is open at the bottom. One account reads the graph as a person leaving an opening; another identifies it as a covered vessel associated with 盍. The visible form does not settle these competing interpretations.
items.alt: Black glyph with a narrow upright stroke and branching arms above an open-bottom lower enclosure.
items.selection_reason: It shows the early graph at the center of competing readings, while its ambiguous outline makes clear that its original depiction remains uncertain.

items.caption: This Shuowen small-seal form has branching upper strokes above an enclosure open at the bottom. Shuowen explains 去 as people parting and parses it as 大 plus phonetic 凵; another analysis disputes that parsing, so the later form does not resolve the early graph’s identity.
items.alt: Black small-seal glyph with branching upper strokes above an enclosure open at the bottom.
items.selection_reason: It illustrates the recorded small-seal form and the explanation attributed to Shuowen, alongside the dispute over that analysis.

limitations.text: The oracle graph’s identity remains disputed: it has been interpreted as a person leaving an opening or as a covered vessel associated with 盍. Departure is not securely established in the oracle-bone examples discussed, and the proposed link from covering to departure is an interpretation rather than a documented sequence.
